title: Make Vertex AI model configurable (GOOGLE_VERTEX_MODEL) – hardcoded gemini-3-flash-preview is global-only, breaking EU data residency
body:
### Describe the improvement you are suggesting in detail


**Problem**
The AI recipient & field detection feature hardcodes the model
`gemini-3-flash-preview`. The self-hosting docs suggest setting
`GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION` to an EU region for data residency ("switch to a
supported region"), but the hardcoded model is not served by ANY regional
EU endpoint – verified empirically against all eight EU regions with a
valid, working API key (control call on global succeeds):

| Location          | HTTP |
|-------------------|------|
| global            | 200  |
| europe-west1      | 404  |
| europe-west3      | 404  |
| europe-west4      | 404  |
| europe-west8      | 404  |
| europe-west9      | 404  |
| europe-north1     | 404  |
| europe-central2   | 404  |
| europe-southwest1 | 404  |

So the only working configuration is the global endpoint, which provides no
data residency guarantees – a blocker for GDPR/EU-compliance-focused
deployments (full document page images are sent to the model).

**Proposal**
Add an optional env var `GOOGLE_VERTEX_MODEL` (default: current model, no
breaking change). EU self-hosters could then pick a GA Gemini model that is
served from EU regions and keep all processing inside the EU. Bonus:
future-proofs the feature, since Google has already shipped GA successors
(Gemini 3.5/3.6 Flash) and the preview model will be deprecated.

Happy to test a PR against our production instance.
